paragraphs: I am applying for the Associate, Corporate Development role at Crusoe. I am completing an MBA in Finance (STEM) at Fordham Gabelli after roles in capital allocation at JPMorgan Asset Management and Lenovo, and the economics of AI infrastructure are where I want to build my career. Crusoe's view that power is the bottleneck for AI compute, and its decision to own the stack from energy to cloud, is the thesis I find most compelling in the market.

My most relevant work is in energy finance and valuation. For Nautilus Solar, I built project- and portfolio-level models for a 6-project, 35.4 MW Illinois portfolio, compared senior debt, sustainability-linked loan and green loan + ABS structures, and recommended a phased green loan + ABS strategy that reduced sponsor equity by $11.1M and improved levered IRR from 8.58% to 9.79%. I have also built a DCF, an LBO and trading comps for J.M. Smucker and screened packaged-food M&A precedents in Capital IQ, the same toolkit your team applies to targets across digital infrastructure and energy.

At JPMorgan Asset Management I built models evaluating $10M in capital deployment scenarios and wrote executive-level investment memos for senior leadership, and at Lenovo I ran scenario and sensitivity analysis that improved capital efficiency by 15%. I would bring that discipline to Crusoe's market maps, screening memos and diligence work, and I would welcome the chance to discuss how I can contribute to the team.
